artists.biography: Beth Gibbons (born 4 January 1965) is an English singer and songwriter best known as the singer and lyricist for the English band Portishead. With Adrian Utley, Gibbons and Barrow released the first Portishead album, Dummy, in 1994 and have produced two other studio albums, a live album, and various singles in the years since. She has also collaborated on a separate project with former Talk Talk bassist Paul Webb (Rustin Man). (Before she joined Geoff Barrow in Portishead, she auditioned for the singer's slot in .O.rang, the group formed by Webb after Talk Talk's late-Eighties departure from EMI, but Portishead's sudden success pre-empted matters.) In October 2002, they released the album Out of Season in the United Kingdom. The album peaked at number 28 in the UK Albums Chart. It was released in the United States a year later.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2002 on Go! Beat and Island Records, Out of Season is a collaborative album between Beth Gibbons, best known as the lead singer of Portishead, and Rustin Man (Paul Webb), former bassist of Talk Talk. Musically, the album stands apart from Gibbons’ work with Portishead, trading trip-hop and electronic textures for a more organic blend of rock, folk, and jazz influences. The sound is often sparse and atmospheric, with subtle arrangements that highlight Gibbons’ haunting vocals and introspective lyrics. The album draws inspiration from artists like Billie Holiday, Nick Drake, and Burt Bacharach, resulting in a moody, melancholic atmosphere that bridges indie rock and torch song traditions.

Out of Season occupies a unique place in Beth Gibbons’ discography, serving as her first major project outside Portishead and showcasing her versatility as a vocalist and songwriter. The album features contributions from Portishead bandmates Adrian Utley and Clive Deamer, as well as Talk Talk’s Lee Harris, further grounding it in the legacy of both groups. Upon its original release, Out of Season received strong critical acclaim for its emotional depth and understated elegance, with reviewers praising its “gorgeously uneasy listening” quality. It also achieved modest commercial success, reaching the UK Top 30 and solidifying Gibbons’ reputation as a distinctive voice in alternative rock.
